briefing.text: These tables appear to hold no outcome data: there is no data_clinical_patient.txt, and the sample table is reported to contain only IDs, oncotree code, somatic status and TMB. Grep every file header for OS/PFS/TTFT/TTT/STATUS/MONTHS columns to confirm. If no outcome column exists, a direct survival or progression test cannot be run. That alone does not make the hypothesis 'Not verifiable'. Under the task's convention, that label applies only when the hypothesis concerns a disease, cohort or data type these tables do not cover. Check whether this cohort is CLL (CANCER_TYPE / ONCOTREE_CODE, CLL_ sample IDs) and whether SF3B1 was sequenced. If both hold, the hypothesis is about this study and the label must be True or False, decided from established CLL biology. State in your reasoning that biology, not a direct test, decided it.
briefing.reason: This is the main way the label goes wrong for this task: missing outcome columns invite a wrong 'Not verifiable'.

briefing.text: Confirm that the study measured SF3B1: look for Hugo_Symbol == SF3B1 in data_mutations.txt, note hotspot calls such as K700E, and count carriers among profiled samples. Define mutant status from nonsynonymous calls only (Missense, Nonsense, Frame_Shift, Splice_Site, In_Frame indels). Do not count Silent, Intron, UTR or Splice_Region rows. Treat every sample listed in data_gene_panel_matrix.txt that has no call as wild-type. The lack of survival data is not evidence for or against the hypothesis. If the label rests on prior knowledge, weigh what the CLL literature (for example the 2011-2015 CLL sequencing studies) has reported about SF3B1 and clinical course.
briefing.reason: This shows the gene is in scope for the study, sets a correct mutant definition, and keeps the absence of data from being read as a negative result.

briefing.text: Do not use TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS or any other non-outcome sample feature as a stand-in for 'disease progression'. Mutational burden is not a progression measure. Only time-to-event, treatment or survival variables can test the claim. If only such proxies exist, do not build a progression test from them.
briefing.reason: This stops an invalid proxy analysis from deciding the label.

briefing.text: If any outcome-like variable does turn up, remember that the SF3B1 effect in CLL is confounded by IGHV mutational status, TP53/del(17p), ATM/del(11q) and stage. SF3B1 is enriched in IGHV-unmutated cases. Check co-occurrence of SF3B1 with TP53, ATM and NOTCH1 in the MAF, and report both univariate and adjusted estimates. Mutant groups are small (about 5-15% of CLL), so a non-significant result here is underpowered and does not on its own contradict the hypothesis.
briefing.reason: This only matters if an outcome variable exists, but it prevents misreading a small, confounded test.

shared_assumptions: Both teams assume the dataset is the source study of the hypothesis (a 105-exome Oviedo CLL cohort) and therefore that the label must be True/False decided from that study's reported finding and literature, not Not verifiable.
Both assume the hypothesis is stated in the same direction as the published finding (not a reversed version), so the literature direction maps directly to True.
Both treat 'disease progression' as equivalent to shorter time to treatment / poorer survival as reported in CLL literature.
unused_evidence: TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS was used only descriptively by team B and deliberately ignored by team A; correctly, since it is not a progression measure.
Read-count columns (t_alt_count, n_alt_count) were not used to verify that the SF3B1 calls are somatic and well supported; this cannot change the label but could change the carrier count.
SOMATIC_STATUS (Matched) was not discussed; it confirms tumour-normal calling and is not outcome evidence.
unresolved_weak_points: Both teams name the same weakest point: no direct test of progression is possible, so the label rests on recalled literature. This is inherent to the data and cannot be resolved from the tables; it was reported, not resolved.
Team A flagged that NOTCH1 has 0 nonsynonymous calls (possibly a filtered MAF) but did not follow it up; this matters only for the carrier counts, not for the label.
second_readings: 'Faster disease progression' could mean shorter time to first treatment, shorter progression-free survival after therapy, or shorter overall survival. The CLL literature reports SF3B1 as adverse on time-to-treatment and survival measures, so every reading points the same way.
The hypothesis could be a reversed version of a reported finding, but its direction (faster) matches what CLL sequencing studies of this period reported, so a reversal reading is not supported.
challenge.verdict: High trust in 'True': the cohort is clearly CLL, SF3B1 is measured and recurrently mutated, and the hypothesis matches the direction the CLL literature reports (adverse clinical course in SF3B1-mutated cases). Neither team could test progression directly, but under the benchmark convention that cannot be resolved from the data.

In chronic lymphocytic leukemia, what clinical-outcome associations have been reported for SF3B1 mutations (time to first treatment, progression-free survival, overall survival), and in which direction?
questions.why: Both teams rely on recalled literature for the label. Independent confirmation of the reported direction would settle the only remaining uncertainty.

findings.question: In chronic lymphocytic leukemia, what clinical-outcome associations have been reported for SF3B1 mutations (time to first treatment, progression-free survival, overall survival), and in which direction?
findings.answer: The web did not settle this: every research call (search and contents) failed with HTTP 403/502 from the gateway, so no page was read. From recalled literature only, not verified: SF3B1 mutations in CLL are consistently reported as an adverse marker. They are linked to shorter time to first treatment (Wang et al. NEJM 2011; Quesada et al. Nat Genet 2012), shorter progression-free survival after chemoimmunotherapy (trial analyses such as CLL8 and UK LRF CLL4), and shorter overall survival (Rossi et al. Blood 2011; Oscier et al. Blood 2013). The effect is partly independent of IGHV status. That direction supports 'faster progression' (leans True), but the web did not confirm it.
